It is anti-ship, not anti-aircraft, and is integrated at Hyderabad, not Mumbai.

q: BrahMos supersonic cruise missile is developed by the joint efforts of
explanation: BrahMos is a joint venture of India's DRDO (50.5%) and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya (49.5%), set up under a 1998 inter-governmental agreement.

notes.text: - **Joint venture of India and Russia:** **DRDO 50.5%** + **NPO Mashinostroyeniya (NPOM), Russia 49.5%** = **BrahMos Aerospace**, created by an Inter-Governmental Agreement signed in **Moscow, 1998** (not USA, France, Israel, Japan, China).

q: Which of the following is a supersonic missile?
explanation: BrahMos is the supersonic (cruise) missile; Agni and Prithvi are ballistic missiles.

q: The supersonic anti-ship cruise missile BrahMos was successfully test-fired for the 3rd time on 12 February 2003. Where are these missiles manufactured?
explanation: BrahMos missiles are integrated at the BrahMos Integration Complex, Kanchanbagh, Hyderabad (later also Thiruvananthapuram and Lucknow); not Ludhiana, Dehradun or Bengaluru.

explanation: BrahMos was designed primarily as an anti-ship (and land-attack) supersonic cruise missile; it is not anti-tank, anti-aircraft or a satellite.

explanation: BrahMos was (and is) produced at the BrahMos Integration Complex, Hyderabad, the venture's first production unit. Bangalore is wrong; the parallel copy of this APPSC 2003 question is keyed Hyderabad.

q: On 26 March 2003 India successfully test-fired the Prithvi missile from Chandipur-on-Sea. On the same day Pakistan also test-fired a missile of the same capability. What is its name?
explanation: On 26 March 2003, hours after India's Prithvi test from Chandipur, Pakistan test-fired the short-range Abdali (Hatf-II) missile.

q: What is the name of the Medium Range Surface to Air Missile jointly developed by India and Israel?
explanation: Barak-8 (MRSAM) is the medium-range surface-to-air missile developed jointly by DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries. BrahMos is India-Russia, Pinaka a rocket launcher.

q: Which of the following DRDO's missiles is used to destroy enemy radars and communication facilities?
explanation: Anti-radiation missiles (DRDO's Rudram-I, from the Su-30MKI) home on radar emissions to destroy enemy radars and communication sites; Akash is a SAM, Trishul a short-range SAM and Nag an anti-tank missile.
